# Incident Report — MTA 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.17.0.99 (DHCP-assigned by 172.17.0.17) |
| MAC address | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT |
| AD domain | bepositive.com (NetBIOS: BEPOSITIVE) |
| Logged-in user account | afletcher (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, realm BEPOSITIVE.COM) |

Corroborating evidence: DHCP Discover/Request frames carry `dhcp.option.hostname = DESKTOP-RNVO9AT` from MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4; NBNS name-registration broadcasts from 172.17.0.99 advertise both `BEPOSITIVE<00>` and `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00/20>`; Kerberos traffic to the domain controller (172.17.0.17, WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com) shows CNameString `afletcher`.

## Malware Family
**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer). Attribution is **signature-confirmed**: the exported alert log contains the ETPRO rule `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2`, firing 48 times against the same host/port/URI pattern observed independently in the raw PCAP (repeated `POST /foots.php` to 79.124.78.197:80). This is reinforced behaviorally by:
- A fixed, spoofed legacy user agent on every C2 request (`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)`), matching the ET rule `GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser`.
- A gate check-in/response protocol consistent with loader/stealer C2 kits: `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` returns the plaintext body `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` — a pipe-delimited bot-ID/campaign-ID/callback-URL tuple — followed immediately by a `POST /index.php` (105-byte body) and then 96 periodic `POST /foots.php` beacons (`Content-Type: application/octet-stream`) over the remainder of the capture.

## Infection Chain (as observed)
1. `172.17.0.99:49806/49813 → 46.254.34.201:443`, TLS Client Hello SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` — two back-to-back TLS sessions (17:35:04 and 17:35:09 UTC) pull down 212,640 bytes and 461,389 bytes respectively from the server to the client (~674 KB total). This is the likely payload-staging/download channel; because it is TLS-encrypted and no key log is present in the evidence, the exact filename and hash of the retrieved payload cannot be extracted from this capture.
2. Within seconds of the second TLS session, C2 activity to 79.124.78.197 begins (first `POST /foots.php` at 17:35:07 UTC) — consistent with execution of a freshly downloaded loader immediately establishing C2.
3. Ongoing beaconing (`POST /foots.php`, ~40–112 bytes, `application/octet-stream`) continues every 60–90 seconds for the remainder of the capture (last observed beacon frame 5077, ~19 minutes after capture start of this activity).

Note: alert-log entries for `GPL NETBIOS SMB Session Setup NTMLSSP...overflow`, `SMB IPC$ unicode share access`, and `SMB_COM_TRANSACTION Max Data Count of 0` (172.17.0.99 → 172.17.0.17, port 139) and `GPL RPC kerberos principal name overflow` (port 88) reflect ordinary Windows/AD SMBv1 and Kerberos negotiation traffic between the workstation and its domain controller. These are legacy signature false-positives on normal authentication traffic, not evidence of exploitation, and are not treated as IOCs below.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- `79.124.78.197:80` (HTTP) — Koi Stealer C2 endpoint, confirmed by ETPRO signature and observed check-in/beacon traffic.
- `46.254.34.201:443` (TLS) — payload delivery/staging host, SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`.

**Malicious domain**
- `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (resolved via TLS SNI to 46.254.34.201; no corresponding DNS query was captured for this name, meaning the client connected via a hardcoded IP/SNI rather than local DNS resolution).

**Malicious URLs / URIs**
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` (initial gate check-in, GET)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` (POST, 105-byte body — likely exfil/config exchange)
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` (repeated POST beacon, ×96 over the capture)

**Bot / campaign identifiers**
- Bot ID: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn`
- Campaign/sub-ID: `qIOuKk7U`

**Transferred file names / hashes**
- None recoverable. All bulk data transfer associated with the intrusion (the two ~200 KB/460 KB downloads from 46.254.34.201) occurred over TLS with no key-log material in the evidence set, so no file name or SHA256 hash can be extracted from this capture. No cleartext executable, DLL, or archive transfer was observed anywhere else in the PCAP; the only other file objects recovered via HTTP export (`connecttest.txt` from Microsoft NCSI, `ProcessMAU.txt` from the legitimate Adobe ARM telemetry domain `acroipm2.adobe.com`, and Windows Update `.cab` trust-list files) are benign OS/AV housekeeping traffic, not malware artifacts.
